title: 63% of Europe’s new data centre capacity is now going somewhere other than the big five
summary:
Europe’s data centre capacity will reach 13 gigawatts by the end of 2026, a fifth more than last year, and most of the new supply is no longer landing where the industry has always built.
Of the roughly 700 megawatts added in the second quarter, only 37% went to the five established markets of Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, and Dublin.
The Netherlands separately bans hyperscale projects above 70 megawatts of IT capacity or ten hectares across most of the country.
Installed capacity there reached 439 megawatts at the end of 2025 and the industry association Spain DC forecasts roughly 2,537 megawatts by 2030, with Amazon alone committing €33.7bn in Aragón.
Utilities have spotted the opening, with Uniper committing €5bn to repurpose old power plant sites whose grid connections already exist.

title: The Powerful Chinese AI Model Experts Warned About Is Here
summary:

The new model, GLM 5.3, could be a gift for companies looking to secure their systems against attacks, providing a cheaper way to scan for hidden bugs and other weaknesses.
Alongside the new model, Z.ai released OpenVuln, a service for scanning code repositories for vulnerabilities using GLM 5.3.
Like Anthropic, OpenAI has made its most advanced models available to a limited number of partners prior to full release.

title: OpenAI Pauses Training of New AI Models, Citing Cybersecurity Worries
summary:
ChatGPT maker OpenAI announced on Tuesday that it’s pausing the research and development of its newest AI models.
This is a big course reversal for the firm, which has maintained that it can mitigate the significant cybersecurity risks posed by new AI models.
Researching and training new AI models is a compute-intensive process.
It’s why so many tech companies want to build new data centers, to give them the computing firepower they need, despite widespread backlash.
In other words, it’s possible that OpenAI has decided to pause the training of new AI models because it can simply no longer afford to keep doing so.

summary:

title: Becoming AI-Native Requires the Right People More Than the Right Technology. Here’s the Shift Leaders Need to Make.
summary:
AI adoption is primarily a people challenge, requiring structured experimentation, change management, and new hybrid roles that connect technical capabilities with business needs.
The companies that become AI-native will not be the ones with the longest list of AI tools.
AI adoption is a people challenge firstThere is a persistent misconception that access to AI technology equals transformation.
Human judgment becomes more valuableAs organizations become AI-native, AI shifts from supporting individual solutions to powering shared, repeatable systems, and the leverage compounds.
It is not a limitation to design around but the mechanism that makes AI workflows trustworthy enough to scale.

title: Most Americans under 30 are now more worried than excited about AI
summary:

title: CISA orders a three-day patch after a flaw in the Ray AI framework comes under active attack
summary:
The bug, tracked as CVE-2025-62593, is a code-injection weakness that can hand an attacker remote code execution on a vulnerable Ray deployment.
In plain terms, someone who has never logged in could get a target’s machine to run commands of their choosing.
Ray is maintained by Anyscale and sits at the heart of modern machine-learning pipelines, distributing Python workloads across clusters of CPUs and GPUs.
Anyscale has fixed the issue in Ray version 2.52.0, so the operators still on earlier releases are the ones exposed.
That earlier flaw is not the one CISA listed this week, but it is a preview of what exposed Ray infrastructure attracts, from cryptojacking that quietly hijacks hardware to outright data theft.

title: Tiny quantum engines reveal useful energy hiding in “waste heat”
summary:
What counts as heat, and what qualifies as useful work when a machine is made from only an atom and particles of light?
Some of the energy carried by that escaping light can still be used to perform useful work on another quantum system.
Their latest study examined what happens to this distinction between heat and useful energy when the system approaches the semi-classical limit.
Separating Useful Energy From HeatIn the semi-classical limit, the atom inside the cavity continues to be treated as a quantum system with discrete energy levels.
The findings show how a better understanding of the boundary between heat and useful work could help researchers take advantage of energy that might otherwise appear to be lost.

title: LG’s $2 Billion lansing battery plant is now building cells
summary:
